body.content: Counterfactual: What if the checklist is not authored by an expert but crowd-evolved (e.g., Delphi with feedback on verifiable outcomes)? Then the 'checklist is a lossy compression of the expert' objection weakens: the checklist could exceed any single expert's cue-set. But the compliance-tracking problem remains: panelists may comply with a rich checklist yet still fail on cases requiring configural integration. So even a crowd-evolved checklist does not guarantee genuine reliability; it only shifts the bias boundary. The distinguishing evidence would still be structured errors on interaction-heavy items.
body.possible_next_move: Specify the minimal configural task that a flat checklist cannot solve and test whether panelists spontaneously add configural judgment.
body.why_keep_this: It blocks the easy refutation that a better-authored checklist solves the problem, by showing the configural-integration issue is orthogonal to authorship.
